discussion.title: A measured strength–toughness tradeoff within one steel study
discussion.text: In the AISI 4340 tempering series, the 180 °C condition has yield strength 1550 MPa and reported KIc 55 MPa √m; at 500 °C these are 1185 MPa and 127.72 MPa √m. This source-specific treatment comparison shows increasing toughness with lower yield strength. It is not evidence for a universal static tradeoff or a change in dynamic spall performance.

discussion.title: Copper shows co-improvement, with a provisional toughness qualification
discussion.text: Within the Cu DPD series, DPD0.4 has measured yield strength 362 MPa and provisional KQ 24 MPa √m; DPD2 has 589 MPa and 30.8 MPa √m. Both reported quantities increase over these conditions. KQ is conditional and is not relabeled as validated KIc; these specimens are not matched to the dynamic Cu records.

discussion.title: Static and dynamic maps ask different questions
discussion.text: The classical view compares measured yield strength with reported fracture toughness. The dynamic view compares a shock elastic threshold with a tensile failure stress. Fracture toughness also depends on crack geometry and constraint; spall depends on loading history, microstructure, defects and rate. No universal KIc-to-spall or static-yield-to-HEL equivalence is assumed.

discussion.title: Coverage limits the comparison
discussion.text: The reviewed primary seed contains 13 same-context yield/toughness pairs, 47 measured yield values and 70 toughness values. It contains 0 explicitly matched same-specimen four-property comparisons. Class locations across differently sampled maps cannot establish that a material improves or deteriorates under shock. Separate marginals and alternative measured-property panels expose the gaps.

discussion.title: Methods must remain visible
discussion.text: Compressive and tensile yield strengths are labeled separately. Conditional KQ and indentation estimates remain distinguishable from qualifying notched KIc measurements; Charpy energy is never converted into KIc. Flexural or compressive failure strength is never substituted for yield strength.

discussion.title: A loading landscape is not a causal model
discussion.text: HEL and spall are excluded from the loading-feature distances and may be used only as response overlays. Peak shock stress and tensile rate can covary with material, paper and experimental method. Spall and tensile rate may share the same velocity-history reduction. Pooled correlations, within-paper correlations, paper medians and leave-one-paper-out ranges describe associations, not effects.

discussion.title: Neighborhoods can follow source and sampling
discussion.text: Every embedding reports same-source neighbor concentration against its random-label baseline, neighbor preservation, and seed or kernel sensitivity. High same-source concentration warns that the map may distinguish laboratories or loading windows rather than intrinsic material families. Isolated islands and axis directions have no independent physical meaning.

discussion.title: The outcome landscape is descriptive
discussion.text: The HEL–spall embedding reuses the two dynamic responses, so it cannot discover which static parameters control those responses. Its class separation is not independent evidence of a mechanism. The elastic-property cohort shows only static relationships until matched dynamic measurements are added.

methods.title: Admission and joining
methods.text: Only primary experimental values reviewed against XML table cells and method paragraphs are used from ZAKI. Joins require the same source, experiment identifier, material label and processing group. Ambiguous repeated property values are held instead of averaged. Alternative reductions are excluded. Canonical dynamic records preserve their documented extraction level; no inferred HEL or synthetic cross-paper pair enters the outcome embedding.

methods.title: Scaling and missingness
methods.text: Each cohort uses complete finite observations in its explicitly listed features. Positive stresses, rates and elastic moduli are log10 transformed, then each input is centered and divided by its population standard deviation. Poisson ratio remains linear. Constant columns are discarded. No zero fill, mean imputation or mixing of incompatible property dimensions is performed.

methods.title: UMAP
methods.text: Genuine umap-learn UMAP with Euclidean metric, 2 components, n_neighbors=min(10,n−1), min_dist=0.15, spectral initialization, seed 42 and one worker. Sensitivity runs use seed 7 and neighbor counts 5 and 15, capped by cohort size. Coordinates are computed on the server and exported unchanged.

methods.title: Diffusion maps
methods.text: Dense Gaussian Kij=exp(−dij²/epsilon), epsilon=median nonzero squared distance; alpha=1 density normalization, then a row-stochastic Markov operator. The symmetric conjugate is eigendecomposed, stationary mode removed, and coordinates are lambda^t psi with t=1. Sensitivity uses epsilon factors 0.5 and 2 and t=2. Dense kernels include diagonal self-affinity.

methods.title: Diagnostics
methods.text: Neighbor preservation is mean overlap of the 7 nearest neighbors in standardized input and embedding space. Stability is the corresponding neighbor overlap between parameter runs. Same-source concentration is measured in embedding neighbors; its random baseline is sum_s n_s(n_s−1)/(N(N−1)). Ties use stable input order and can affect duplicate-vector neighborhoods. Spearman ranks average ties. No significance or causal claim is made.
